### 3. bl-0005

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Confirmed against the locked Pyright 1.1.411 (`uv.lock:737-738`; `pyproject.toml:18` only requires `>=1.1.409`). Three backend methods treat a `-32601 Unhandled method` reply as success with an empty result: `get_selection_range` at `src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/pyright_lsp.py:1022-1024`, `get_inlay_hints` at `pyright_lsp.py:1244-1246` and `get_semantic_tokens` at `pyright_lsp.py:1303-1305` each do `if is_unhandled_method_error(response): return []` (the predicate is at `src/python_refactor_mcp/util/lsp_converters.py:148-157`). The client never records the server's advertised capabilities. `start()` (`pyright_lsp.py:354-392`) and the restart path (`pyright_lsp.py:243-265`) both send `initialize` and check only for `"error"`, then drop `response["result"]["capabilities"]`. So an unsupported feature looks the same as "no data". The damage spreads: `apply_type_annotations` pulls hints only through `pyright.get_inlay_hints` (`src/python_refactor_mcp/tools/refactoring/type_annotations.py:64`), gets `[]`, and reports `"No inferable type annotations found"` (`type_annotations.py:88-94`). That is a false negative. The integration tests at `tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py:407-429` and `:485-515` assert only `isinstance(payload, list)`, so the silent `[]` passes CI. The row is confirmed as written. |
| Approach | Use an explicit unsupported error. Two alternatives were rejected: (a) hiding the tools from `tools/list` is not viable, because the tool list is static at registration (`tool_registry.py:1767-1786`) while capabilities are known only per workspace after Pyright starts, and removing the tools would break the public contract (addenda Contract posture); (b) an AST fallback is a second regression shape. It is credible only for `selection_range` (mirror the folding-range AST fallback), so it is proposed as a spin-off (see Risks). Changes: (1) `src/python_refactor_mcp/errors.py`: add `LspFeatureUnsupportedError(PyrightError)` with `code = "LSP_UNSUPPORTED"` and a ClassVar `caller_summary` telling the caller that the running Pyright language server does not implement this LSP feature for this tool, that no data is available from this backend, and not to retry. It reaches the caller through the existing `tool_error_boundary` -> `_translate_backend_error` path (`src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_runtime.py:216-234,259-260`) with no boundary change. (2) `pyright_lsp.py`: extract the duplicated initialize handshake from `start()` and `restart()` into one `_initialize_session()` helper that also stores `self._server_capabilities: JSONDict \| None` (initialized to `None` in `__init__` at `pyright_lsp.py:167-179`). Add `_require_capability(provider_key, method)`, which raises `LspFeatureUnsupportedError` when capabilities were recorded and `provider_key` (`selectionRangeProvider` / `inlayHintProvider` / `semanticTokensProvider`) is absent or falsy. When capabilities are `None` (the unit-test harness never initializes), skip the pre-check. In each of the three methods, call `_require_capability` before `_request` and replace `return []` in the unhandled-method branch with `raise LspFeatureUnsupportedError(<method>)`. Leave the other 10 unhandled-method branches unchanged (Risks). (3) `apply_type_annotations` gets no code change: the raise propagates, so the tool states why it cannot annotate (Acceptance option 2). A rewrite that stops depending on inlay hints is a separate feature and is recommended as a spin-off row. |
| Scope | Production files: 2. `src/python_refactor_mcp/errors.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/pyright_lsp.py`. Test files: 3 (extended, 0 new). `tests/unit/test_pyright_lsp.py`: capabilities recorded from the `initialize` result; a capability absent after initialize raises `LspFeatureUnsupportedError` without sending the request; a `-32601` reply raises for all three methods; the existing positive inlay and semantic tests at `:600-640` stay green through the `None`-capabilities path. `tests/unit/test_refactoring_tools.py`: `apply_type_annotations` propagates `LspFeatureUnsupportedError` instead of returning an empty preview. `tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py`: `test_inlay_and_semantic_tokens` and the `selection_range` half of `test_type_hierarchy_and_selection_range_tools` assert either a non-empty payload or `is_error` with `[LSP_UNSUPPORTED]` in the text, never a bare `isinstance(list)`. Add `changelog.d/fixed-bl-0005.md` (excluded from the count). No deletions. Within Rule 3 and Rule 4 targets; no exemption claimed. |

### 5. bl-0007

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Confirmed, root cause is an argument-shape mismatch plus a success check that cannot fail. `src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/pyright_lsp.py:1389-1410` sends `workspace/executeCommand pyright.createtypestub` with `arguments=[package_name]` (or `[package_name, output_dir]`) and returns `True` whenever the response has no `error` key. Installed Pyright 1.1.411 (`.venv/Lib/site-packages/pyright/dist/dist/pyright-internal.js`, module `1190` `CreateTypeStubCommand.execute`) returns early (`undefined`, so `result:null`) when `arguments.length<2`. It reads `arguments[0]` as the workspace-root URI, `arguments[1]` as the import name and `arguments[2]` as an optional file URI. Our 1-arg call is therefore a no-op, and the 2-arg call treats `output_dir` as the import name. Even with the right shape, the command never produces a JSON-RPC error: `createTypeStub` catches every failure and sends it to `console.error` + `window.showErrorMessage`, and the result is always `null`. So "no error key" can never tell success from failure. Pyright has no output-dir parameter. `getTypeStubTargetInfo` fixes the output at `configOptions.stubPath ?? <projectRoot>/typings`, plus `/<first import segment>`. The CLI path in the same bundle (`--createstub <IMPORT>` sets `languageServerSettings.typeStubTargetImportName`) is synchronous and headless: it prints `Type stub was created for '<x>'` and resolves `NoErrors`, or prints `Error occurred when creating type stub: Import '<x>' could not be resolved` and resolves `FatalError`. `src/python_refactor_mcp/tools/analysis/type_stubs.py:14-26` is a pass-through Protocol that returns `bool`. `src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_registry.py:329-334` returns that `bool`, and its description says neither where stubs land nor that the tool writes immediately. Adjacent: `output_dir` is not in `PATH_PARAMS` (`src/python_refactor_mcp/tool_runtime.py:32-39`), so today it is not checked against the workspace boundary. |
| Approach | Replace the LSP route with the Pyright CLI, which is headless, reports failures through its exit code, and is already a declared dependency (`pyproject.toml` `pyright>=1.1.409`). (1) `tools/analysis/type_stubs.py`: rewrite `create_type_stubs(config, package_name, output_dir)`. Validate `package_name` as a dotted identifier and raise the bl-0002 caller-safe error otherwise. Resolve the output root as `output_dir` or, when omitted, `<workspace_root>/typings` (Pyright's `stubPath` default, where the running language server picks stubs up). Check it with `validate_workspace_path` (`util/shared.py:112`). If `<root>/<top-segment>` already exists, refuse with a caller-safe error. Run `asyncio.create_subprocess_exec(sys.executable, "-m", "pyright", "--createstub", package_name, "--pythonpath", str(config.python_executable), cwd=<tempdir>)` with an argv list (no shell), mirroring `tools/refactoring/lint_fix.py:50-60`. On a non-zero exit, raise a caller-safe error that carries Pyright's `Error occurred when creating type stub: ...` line. On exit 0, glob `<tempdir>/typings/<top>/**/*.pyi` (or `<top>.pyi`). If there are none, raise a caller-safe error ("Pyright produced no stub files for '<pkg>'"). Otherwise move the tree into the output root and return the created absolute paths. (2) `models.py`: add `TypeStubCreationResult{package_name, output_dir, files: list[str]}` next to `TypeStubFreshnessResult` (`models.py:475`). (3) `tool_registry.py:329-334`: return the model and pass `app.config`. ### 8. bl-0010

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Confirmed. (1) `get_symbol_outline`: the MCP wrapper `src/python_refactor_mcp/server.py:172-174` sets `effective_limit = 500` for workspace scans. `src/python_refactor_mcp/tools/navigation/outline.py:188` passes that to `apply_limit`, which slices top-level roots only, so every root's `children` subtree is unbounded (audit: 500 roots / 9,933 nodes / 7.5 MB). (2) `get_module_dependencies` (`tool_registry.py:1316-1332` -> `tools/metrics/dependencies.py:226-306`) and `code_metrics` (`tool_registry.py:1298-1313` -> `tools/metrics/complexity.py:60-109`) take no limit and return every dependency edge / function (652 KB / 339 KB). `DependencyGraph` (`models.py:555-562`) and `CodeMetricsResult` (`models.py:535-543`) have no `truncated` field. (3) `search_symbols` (`tool_registry.py:1185`) and `dead_code_detection` (`tool_registry.py:1224-1233`) already support `limit` and `truncated` (`tools/search/symbols.py:57-61`, `tools/search/dead_code.py:189-197`), but default to `limit=None`, so they are unbounded by default. The root cause is the same across all five tools: no default payload bound at the tool surface, and for the outline the bound counts the wrong unit. |

Add optional fields `truncated: bool = False` + `total_functions` (already present) to `CodeMetricsResult`, and `truncated: bool = False` + `total_dependencies: int = 0` to `DependencyGraph`. All new fields default so the existing construction sites at `complexity.py:102` and `dependencies.py:300` still compile. (b) `outline.py:get_symbol_outline`: add a `max_nodes: int \| None` parameter. After sort/offset/`limit`, walk roots in order, counting 1 + descendants per root. Stop adding roots once the budget is spent, and prune the children of the root that crosses the budget depth-first. Return `SymbolOutlineResult(items, total_count=<roots pre-slice>, offset, truncated, total_nodes, returned_nodes)`. Keep `limit` meaning top-level roots (no semantic change to an existing parameter). (c) `server.py:158-187`: change the return type to `SymbolOutlineResult`. Add `max_nodes: int \| None = None`, which resolves to 250 when `file_path` and `file_paths` are both None (mirror the existing `effective_limit` pattern at `server.py:172-174`; 250 nodes is about 190 KB at the audit's ~755 B/node). Update the docstring. (d) `complexity.py:code_metrics` / `dependencies.py:get_module_dependencies`: add `limit: int \| None = None` (internal default stays unbounded so `metrics/architecture.py:38` and `refactoring/circular_imports.py:421`, which need the full graph for cycle and layer analysis, are unaffected). code_metrics computes aggregates (`total_functions`, `avg_cyclomatic`, `max_cyclomatic`) before capping, sorts `functions` by cyclomatic desc then path/line so hotspots survive, and applies `util/shared.py:apply_limit`. Suggested defaults: 200 functions, 500 edges, 200 symbols, 200 dead-code items. The executor calibrates each so a scan of this repo's `src/` stays under ~200 KB, and states the default in each docstring along with how to page or raise it. |

### 10. bl-0012

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| Route | deepen |
| Diagnosis | Row confirmed; the root cause is in rope's changer config. `src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/rope_backend.py:98-101` `_build_inline_default` returns `ArgumentDefaultInliner(op.index)` as-is. rope's `ArgumentDefaultInliner.__init__` sets `self.remove = False` (`.venv/Lib/site-packages/rope/refactor/change_signature.py:262-272`), and `change_definition_info` clears the default only when `remove` is true. So call sites get the inlined value, but `_FunctionChangers.change_definition` re-emits the def with the default still in it. The repo's LibCST post-pass does not cause the bug: `src/python_refactor_mcp/tools/refactoring/signature_annotations.py:101-116` already marks the `inline_default` target default as blocked and never re-adds it, and `_fill` (`:143`) only fills defaults that are missing, never strips them. Negative index: `SignatureOperation.index` (`src/python_refactor_mcp/models.py:327`) is an unconstrained `int`, and the `argument_default_inliner` wrapper (`src/python_refactor_mcp/server.py:210-221`) passes it straight through. rope then uses Python-style indexing into `args_with_defaults` (`change_signature.py:269-276`), so `-1` quietly targets the last parameter. The fix also exposes a new hazard: once the default is really removed, `def f(a=1, b=2)` at index 1 would come out as `def f(a=1, b)`, which is a SyntaxError. |
| Approach | (1) `rope_backend.py` `_build_inline_default`: build the inliner, set `inliner.remove = True`, return `[inliner]`. rope has no constructor flag for this, and its own deprecated `ChangeSignature.inline_default` (`change_signature.py:123-130`) has the same no-removal behavior. (2) `rope_backend.py` `RopeBackend.change_signature._work`: before `get_changes`, check each `inline_default` op against `ChangeSignature(project, resource, offset).get_args()` (rope public API, `change_signature.py:79-86`, which lists `(name, default)` including `self`, the same positional indexing the post-pass `_positional_params` uses). Reject these with bl-0002's caller-safe input error, naming `index` and the reason: index out of range; target parameter has no default (today a silent no-op); an earlier positional parameter still has a default (the removal would produce invalid syntax). Check against the original args only when `inline_default` is the first op; for later ops in a chained `change_signature`, keep the range check and state the limit in the docstring. (3) `models.py:327`: `index: int or None = Field(default=None, ge=0)`, mirroring `Position.line = Field(ge=0)` at `models.py:11`. This covers `change_signature` (`tool_registry.py:988`), whose `operations: list[SignatureOperation]` is validated by the SDK before the call. (4) `server.py:210-221`: annotate `index` as `Annotated[int, Field(ge=0)]` so the MCP SDK's pre-call argument validation rejects `-1` as a caller-visible `ToolError` (`.venv/Lib/site-packages/mcp/server/mcpserver/tools/base.py:148-152`) and the schema advertises `minimum: 0`. The docstring already promises removal and needs no change. |
| Scope | Production 3: `src/python_refactor_mcp/backends/rope_backend.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/models.py`, `src/python_refactor_mcp/server.py`. Tests 3 (extended): `tests/unit/test_rope_backend.py` (real rope, mirroring `test_change_signature_annotation_restore_end_to_end` at `:30-47`: `def helper(a: int, b: int = 2)` plus a call `helper(1)` at index 1 gives `def helper(a: int, b: int)` and `helper(1, 2)`; rejects no-default target, preceding-default target, and out-of-range index), `tests/unit/test_models.py` (`SignatureOperation(op='inline_default', index=-1)` raises `ValidationError`), `tests/integration/test_end_to_end.py` (`argument_default_inliner` with `index:-1` over `mcp_session` returns `is_error` naming `index`). No deletions. Within Rule 3 and Rule 4 targets. |
| Tool policy | edit-only |

| Risks | Contract posture (addenda): rejecting a negative `index` for every `change_signature` op (`add`/`remove`/`rename`/`inline_default`), and the new no-default and preceding-default rejections, all reject input that used to be accepted, so the PR body must call this out and use a `changed-breaking-bl-0012.md` fragment. Fanout probe (shape C, construction and consumer sites of `SignatureOperation`): Grep over `src/` finds 6 referencing production files (`models.py`, `server.py`, `backends/rope_backend.py`, `tool_registry.py`, `tools/refactoring/signature.py`, `tools/refactoring/signature_annotations.py`); the only constructions are 2 in `server.py:204,220`, and neither passes a negative index; only the 3 scoped files need edits. `signature_annotations.py:101-107` already blocks the default, so no post-pass change is needed; verify with the real-rope test that the annotation is restored with no default.
